q1.question: What are you working on?
q1.notes: SAFETY: Follow site LOTO, electrical PPE, arc-flash, ladder, rotating-equipment, combustion, refrigerant, and life-safety procedures. Never bypass a safety or exceed product ratings. Verify exact model and approved documentation.

q2.question: What BMS panel component are you troubleshooting?

q4.question: Is the specified power supply present and within the voltage range required by the installed power-supply/server hardware?
q4.notes: Do not assume every installation is 24 VAC only. Verify the exact PS-24V/automation-server hardware and approved documentation before testing.

q7.question: Is the transformer reset/trip condition normal?

q8.question: Is the Automation Server status light normal?

q9.question: Can Device Administrator communicate through the AS-P USB device port using a known-good USB data cable?
q9.notes: The front USB device port is intended for Device Administrator/program download. A charging-only cable will not work.

r1.action: Verify source power, disconnect, breakers, and upstream electrical supply.

r2.diagnosis: Automation-server/Central IO supply or backplane power is missing or out of tolerance
r2.action: Verify the installed power-supply model, source voltage, protective devices, terminal-base seating, and backplane connection. Do not energize until the source and polarity/type match the product documentation.

r3.action: Determine cause with safe electrical testing before resetting. Inspect for shorts and overloads.

r4.action: Test fuses, inspect hidden fuse holders and Panduit, then replace only after finding the cause.

r5.action: Confirm transformer VA loading, correct the overload, and reset if permitted.

r6.action: Record LED pattern, verify power quality, allow boot time, and follow controller recovery procedure.
evidence_required: Exact controller model and EBO/firmware version

r7.action: Document controller identity and status in Device Administrator, then verify EBO server association, IP settings, application status, Central IO bus, bindings, and field-bus health.

r8.diagnosis: Automation Server cannot be reached locally
r8.action: Verify USB cable/driver and controller boot state; escalate for recovery or replacement if needed.
evidence_required: Exact controller model and EBO/firmware version

diagnostic_artifacts.BACnet/IP field controller: Device Report, Error Log and Crash Report where supported by exact model/version

q101.question: Is the UI16 status light normal?

q102.question: What kind of input are you troubleshooting?
q102.notes: UI-16 supports digital, counter, supervised, voltage, current, temperature, and resistive inputs. Confirm the configured electrical type before field testing.

q103.question: Is the digital input contact normally open or normally closed?

q104.question: With field wires removed, does jumpering the input change the UI state?

q105.question: With field wires removed, does opening/closing the input change the UI state as expected?

q106.question: At the field device, does simulating the contact change the controller state?

q107.question: Is the current transmitter a two-wire loop-powered device or a separately powered three/four-wire device?
q107.notes: Confirm the installed input supports the transmitter range. Identify loop-powered versus separately powered wiring from the exact device documentation.

q108.question: Is loop DC power present with correct polarity?

q109.question: Is the transmitter power source present and correct?

q110.question: With the loop intact and the meter connected correctly in series, is the expected current measured at the controller terminals?
q110.notes: Never place a current meter directly across a powered source. Follow meter and site electrical-safety procedures.

q111.question: Does measured current correspond to the transmitter range and the actual process value?
q111.notes: Use the transmitter nameplate/configured range. For a 4-20 mA transmitter, calculate expected mA from the configured lower and upper range values.

q112.question: Is expected current present at the field device output?

q114.question: Is the correct device supply present and is the signal common/reference correctly connected?
q114.notes: Confirm the field device supply requirement separately from the 0-10 V signal. Verify whether signal common is isolated or shared.

q115.question: Is expected signal voltage measured at the controller terminals?

q116.question: If the displayed value is unstable, does the voltage also fluctuate on a properly connected meter?

q117.question: Does measured voltage correspond to the expected engineering value?

q118.question: After isolating the field circuit, does a safe known-good 0-10 V test signal make the input respond correctly?
q118.notes: Use an approved signal source. Do not inject voltage into a circuit that is still connected to an active transmitter.

q119.question: Is expected voltage present at the field device output?

q120.question: Does the displayed value match the field measurement and configured scale?

q121.question: At the sensor, is resistance open/OL?

q122.question: At the sensor, is resistance near 0 ohms?

q123.question: Does sensor resistance match the manufacturer-approved 10k Type II curve at the independently measured temperature?
q123.notes: In EBO terminology, verify the configured Type II curve used by the project, commonly shown as 10K CSI / I/NET. Use the exact approved curve for the installed Schneider or BAPI part number.

q124.question: Does resistance measured at the controller match resistance at the sensor?

q125.question: Is the input configured for the exact 10k Type II curve required by the installed sensor?
q125.notes: Do not select a thermistor curve solely because the sensor is nominally 10 kOhm at 25 C. Different 10 kOhm curves are not interchangeable.

q126.question: Is displayed temperature within 2 F of a calibrated thermometer?

q127.question: Is the sensor location or mounting affected by drafts, heat sources, wall cavity air, or poor contact?

q130.question: How does this pressure, flow, or airflow measurement reach the controller?
q130.notes: Identify the signal type from the transmitter label, controller label, submittal, or the input configuration in EBO. Many VAV controllers measure airflow with an onboard pressure sensor, which has no field signal wiring to test.

q131.question: Are the pickup and tubing intact, connected to the documented ports, and free of kinks, moisture and blockage?
q131.notes: Follow the controller manufacturer's procedure for zeroing or calibrating the onboard sensor. Do not assume tubing orientation; verify it against the product documentation.

r130.diagnosis: Sensor signal type is not identified
r130.action: Identify how the measurement reaches the controller from labels, drawings, submittals, and the EBO input configuration before testing. Do not assume a 4-20 mA loop.

r131.diagnosis: Onboard sensor pickup or tubing problem
r131.action: Correct the tubing, pickup, and port connections, remove moisture or blockage, then zero or calibrate the sensor using the manufacturer's procedure. Replace the sensor or controller only after the tubing and calibration are confirmed good.

r101.diagnosis: UI16 module connection or module-health issue
r101.action: Check S-cable/module connections, module power, status LEDs, and controller I/O bus status.

r102.action: Verify the input object, physical channel, signal type, and test with a known-good input/channel.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

r104.diagnosis: Controller and wiring respond to contact simulation
r104.action: Investigate the field contact/device, its power, setup, and mechanical operation.

r105.action: Tone and identify conductors; verify terminations at the correct field device and panel input.

r106.action: Restore correct DC loop power after checking breakers, fuses, polarity, and supply rating.

r107.action: Verify the separate power source and correct voltage type before continuing.

r109.diagnosis: Signal is present in field but absent/different at controller
r109.action: Check continuity, polarity, shorts, grounds, and terminations between device and controller.

r113.diagnosis: Incorrect or missing device supply voltage
r113.action: Correct device power source, polarity, and nominal voltage.

r114.diagnosis: Field transmitter calibration or scaling mismatch
r114.action: Compare output signal to process condition; verify transmitter range and calibrate or replace.

r115.diagnosis: Unstable signal originates at field device
r115.action: Verify device stability, power quality, grounding, shielding, and nearby electrical noise.

r116.diagnosis: Controller scaling, filtering, or point setup issue
r116.action: Verify input type, engineering range, units, filtering, and conversion.

r117.diagnosis: Measured signal does not match expected process value
r117.action: Verify transmitter configuration, sensing tubing/mechanics, calibration, and signal wiring.

r118.diagnosis: Controller input operates with a known-good signal
r118.action: Investigate the field device, its calibration, power, and wiring.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

r119.diagnosis: Field device is not generating the expected signal
r119.action: Verify device power, setup, process connection, and operation; repair or replace.

r120.diagnosis: Input and displayed value appear normal
r120.action: Investigate sequence logic, bindings, graphics, trends, and system operation.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

r121.action: Isolate sensor from wiring; repair open conductors/terminations or replace sensor.

r122.action: Isolate sensor from wiring; locate the short or replace the sensor.

r123.diagnosis: Thermistor, reference measurement, or selected resistance curve does not agree
r123.action: Confirm the actual temperature with a calibrated reference, identify the sensor part number, use its approved resistance table, isolate sensor from wiring, and replace only after confirming the mismatch remains.

r125.action: Configure the EBO input as 10k Type II and verify the reading.

r126.action: Continue with application logic, setpoints, operating mode, and equipment operation.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

r127.action: Correct mounting, seal wall penetrations, improve thermal contact, or relocate the sensor.

q201.question: Is the installed digital-output module (DO8 / DO-FC-8 Form C, or DO12 / DO-FA-12 Form A) identified correctly, online, and healthy?
q201.notes: The 8-channel Schneider Central IO digital-output module is DO-FC-8. Form C provides COM/NO/NC relay contacts. DO-FA-12 is a separate 12-channel Form A module; Form A provides a normally open contact only (no NC). Identify the module from its label before testing, because the contact terminals differ.

q202.question: Is the output commanded ON in EBO?

q203.question: Is the software value overridden/forced, or is an -H module HOA switch in Hand or Off?
q203.notes: On -H modules, physical Hand-Off-Auto position can override normal software control. Follow current Schneider advisories for the installed manufacturing date.

q204.question: Does the channel status LED follow the commanded state?
q204.notes: A channel LED indicates output state, but does not prove external source voltage or load operation.

q205.question: With power isolated as required, does continuity across the relay contact change correctly when the output is commanded (COM to NO/NC on a DO-FC-8, or the Form A contact terminals on a DO-FA-12)?
q205.notes: DO-FC-8 is a dry Form C relay output; DO-FA-12 is a Form A (normally open) relay output. Test the contact state appropriate to the installed module and wiring. Do not assume the module supplies voltage.

q206.question: Can the output be commanded manually after verifying safeties?

q207.question: Is the external control-power source present, correctly rated, and switched through the intended contact conductors (COM/NO/NC on a DO8, or the Form A contact terminals on a DO12) to the field device?
q207.notes: Verify source voltage, common/reference, relay contact selection, load rating, and any interposing relay. Use safe energized testing procedures.

r201.action: Investigate enable logic, schedules, safeties, interlocks, operating mode, and setpoints.

r202.diagnosis: Relay contact or channel does not switch as commanded
r202.action: Verify correct module type (DO8 vs DO12), point type, HOA position, contact terminals (COM/NO/NC on Form C; Form A contact terminals on DO12), and isolated continuity. Compare with a known-good channel without exceeding relay ratings; replace hardware only after isolation.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

r203.diagnosis: DO8/DO12 module or application is not responding
r203.action: Verify module status, I/O bus, application download, channel object, and controller health.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

r204.action: The EBO command, module indication, relay contact, external source, and field wiring are functioning. Continue downstream to interposing relay, starter, contactor, equipment enable circuit, safeties, motor, or mechanical equipment.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

q301.question: Is the AO8 module online and healthy?
q301.notes: RBravo equipment notes: RB-004, RB-008, RB-017

q302.question: What AO-8 electrical output type is configured?
q302.notes: AO-8 supports 0-10 VDC and 0-20 mA. A connected device may be configured to use only the 4-20 mA portion, but the module electrical type remains 0-20 mA.

q303.question: Is the output command changing as expected in EBO?

q304.question: Does measured voltage match the commanded value within the AO-8 accuracy and resolution limits?
q304.notes: AO-8 voltage range is 0-10 VDC; published accuracy is +/-100 mV, resolution 42 mV, and minimum load resistance 5 kohm.

q305.question: Does the same voltage reach the field device?

q306.question: Does the receiving field device respond correctly at low, mid, and high command without exceeding the configured operating range?

q320.question: Is the output command changing as expected in EBO?

q321.question: Can output current be measured safely in series with the load using the correct meter range?
q321.notes: AO-8 current output is 0-20 mA. Published maximum load is 650 ohm. Opening the loop or incorrect meter placement can force an invalid result.

q322.question: Does measured current match the commanded value within the AO-8 accuracy and resolution limits?
q322.notes: Published AO-8 current accuracy is +/-0.2 mA and resolution is 0.1 mA. Compare against the configured output scale, including any 4-20 mA device mapping.

q323.question: Does the expected current reach the field device with the loop within the documented load limits?
q323.notes: Verify polarity, total loop resistance, device input configuration, and whether the receiving device expects 0-20 mA or 4-20 mA.

r301.diagnosis: 0-10 V output does not match command
r301.action: Verify AO signal type, scale, common/reference, loading, point configuration, and module channel.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

r302.action: Investigate receiving-device setup and parameters, linkage, sequence, or mechanical equipment.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

r303.diagnosis: AO-8 current-output test cannot establish a valid loop current
r303.action: Verify AO-8 module health, 0-20 mA point configuration, closed-loop wiring, polarity, meter placement, and total load at or below the published 650 ohm maximum.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

r304.diagnosis: AO-8 current output does not match the commanded value
r304.action: Verify 0-20 mA electrical type, output scaling, polarity, loop resistance, receiving-device range, and channel operation. Compare against published +/-0.2 mA accuracy before condemning the module.
checkout_evidence: Authorized temporary forces released and normal control restored

q401.diagnosis: Equipment or symptom is not covered by this workflow
q401.action: Record equipment identity, reported issue, available evidence and missing checks. Escalate for a reviewed equipment-specific workflow. No fault has been established.

q501.question: Which communication protocol and transport are you troubleshooting?
q501.notes: Identify the configured protocol and physical transport from drawings, device labels and configuration. Controller family alone does not identify the transport. BACnet MS/TP and Modbus RTU are distinct serial protocols; BACnet/IP and Modbus TCP are distinct IP protocols. RBravo equipment notes: RB-004 through RB-018 where applicable.

q502.question: Does the controller have correct power and normal status LEDs?

q503.question: Can Device Administrator communicate locally through the USB device port?
q503.notes: Use a known-good data cable and verify the correct USB device port. Distinguish USB-local access from Ethernet reachability.

q504.question: Are other controllers on the same Ethernet network reachable?

q505.question: Are IP address, subnet mask, gateway, and server associations correct?

q520.question: Are other devices on the same MS/TP trunk online?

q521.question: Is the device MAC address unique?

q522.question: Are baud rate, MAC address range, Max Master, and Max Info Frames appropriate for every MS/TP master on the trunk?
q522.notes: A duplicate MAC or Max Master set below an active master address can prevent token passing. Preserve a consistent supported baud rate across the segment. Baud-rate checks apply only to BACnet MS/TP in this branch. For applicable RP/MP devices, verify model-specific automatic baud detection behavior and whether a previous trunk or baud-rate change requires the approved operator procedure; do not assume continuous adaptation.

q523.question: Does the RS-485 segment have correct polarity, daisy-chain topology, shield practice, biasing/termination, and no shorts/grounds?
q523.notes: Do not add termination arbitrarily. Verify the exact trunk design and device instructions; inspect long stubs, star wiring, grounded conductors, and shield grounding at unintended points.

q524.question: After documenting the trunk, does sectional isolation identify a cable segment or device that disrupts communications?
q524.notes: De-energize or disconnect only as permitted. Reconnect one segment/device at a time and document changes to avoid creating address or topology errors.

q540.question: From an appropriate host on the same routed network, do link status, ARP/IP reachability, and ping results support basic IP connectivity?
q540.notes: Ping can be blocked and is not proof of BACnet service. Use link/ARP/routing evidence together rather than relying on ping alone.

q541.question: Are IP address, subnet, gateway, and VLAN correct and unique?

q542.question: Can the BACnet device be discovered locally using the correct BACnet/IP network and UDP port?
q542.notes: Verify unique BACnet device instance separately from IP address. Local discovery depends on broadcasts and the configured BACnet/IP network/port.

q543.question: Is the client/device on another IP subnet or otherwise dependent on BACnet broadcast management/routing?
q543.notes: BBMD/foreign-device configuration is relevant when BACnet broadcasts must cross IP subnet boundaries; avoid duplicate or unintended broadcast-distribution paths.

q544.question: Are BBMD/BDT/FDT settings and firewall UDP port rules correct?

q560.question: What is dropping offline intermittently on this BACnet MS/TP installation?
q560.notes: Scope the drop before testing: note which devices drop, whether they drop together, and whether the Automation Server itself stays online. Event-log or trend timestamps make the correlation questions in this branch much easier to answer.

q561.question: When the MS/TP devices drop, does the Automation Server itself stay online in EBO with normal status lights and no restart recorded?
q561.notes: If the Automation Server restarts or loses power at the same time, the trunk devices may drop only because the server restarted. Check the Automation Server event log and status lights at the time of a drop before blaming the trunk.

q562.question: Was a device, address, wiring, or program change made on this trunk shortly before the drops started?

q563.question: Does the drop follow one specific device or cable segment (for example it stays with the device when swapped, or clears when that segment is disconnected)?

q564.question: Do the drops coincide with motors or other heavy electrical loads starting or switching, or is the trunk routed alongside power or high-current conductors?
q564.notes: Electrical noise is only one candidate on an MS/TP trunk. Answer Yes only when the timing or the cable routing supports it; otherwise continue to the trunk physical-layer checks.

q565.question: Is a VFD installed on or near this trunk, including a VFD that is itself a device on the trunk?
q565.notes: Answer Yes for any VFD whose output or power wiring runs near the communications cable or shares a panel or enclosure with it, even if the device that is dropping is not the VFD. Answer No if there is no VFD, and the VFD-specific checks will be skipped.

q570.question: At the time of a drop, does the Automation Server record a restart or power loss, or show an abnormal status-light pattern?
q570.notes: Check the event log in Device Administrator or EBO and record the status-light pattern. A restart points to power, firmware, or application causes rather than the network.

q571.question: Is measured or trended Automation Server input power stable during the recorded restart?
q571.notes: Stay within the authorized BMS scope and follow site electrical-safety procedures for any energized measurement.

q572.question: Do other devices on the same switch, VLAN, or uplink also drop from the network at those times?

q573.question: Is the Automation Server IP address static or reserved, unique, and unchanged (no duplicate IP, DHCP lease change, or recent network change)?
q573.notes: Check the Ethernet link lights and, if you have access, the switch-port link history. Coordinate with the site network owner before changing addressing.

q575.question: What do the affected controllers have in common?

q576.question: Do controller resets, voltage dips, or transformer overloads coincide with the drops?

r566.diagnosis: Recent trunk change is the likely trigger
r566.action: Review exactly what changed. Verify unique MAC addresses, consistent baud rate and Max Master settings, and polarity/topology at the changed point. Revert or re-test one change at a time and document each step.

r567.diagnosis: Automation Server restarts while supply power is stable
r567.action: Record the restart reason and time from the event log. Verify firmware and application download state, loading, and recent program changes. Escalate with the logs for the approved recovery or replacement process before swapping hardware.
evidence_required: Exact controller model and EBO/firmware version

diagnostic_artifacts.BACnet/IP field controller: Device Report, Error Log and Crash Report where supported by exact model/version
diagnostic_artifacts.Automation Server: Applicable Automation Server event/restart and diagnostic records; do not assume field-controller export procedures apply

q580.question: Does the value at the controller match the field measurement?

q581.question: Does the supervisory server/graphic value match the controller value?

r501.action: Restore correct power and resolve abnormal LED/startup condition before network troubleshooting.

r502.action: Verify USB connection and boot state; perform approved recovery or replace hardware if required.
evidence_required: Exact controller model and EBO/firmware version

diagnostic_artifacts.BACnet/IP field controller: Device Report, Error Log and Crash Report where supported by exact model/version
diagnostic_artifacts.Automation Server: Applicable Automation Server event/restart and diagnostic records; do not assume field-controller export procedures apply

r503.action: Check switch power/ports, cabling, VLAN, routing, firewall, and upstream network equipment.

r504.action: Verify server association, certificates/time if applicable, controller name/address, and EBO communication settings.

r505.action: Correct IP, subnet, gateway, DNS/server association, and duplicate-address conditions.

r520.action: Check trunk power, master controller port, polarity, topology, termination, shorts, and baud rate.

r521.action: Assign a unique MAC address and recommission the device.

r522.action: Set compatible baud rate and Max Master values across the trunk.

r523.action: Correct polarity, daisy-chain topology, shield grounding, end-of-line termination, shorts, and stubs.

r524.diagnosis: A downstream segment or device is disrupting the trunk
r524.action: Reconnect in sections to isolate the cable/device, then repair wiring or replace the failing transceiver.

r540.action: Verify physical link, switch port, cable, VLAN, subnet, gateway, duplicate IP, and device network settings.

r541.action: Correct addressing/VLAN and coordinate network changes before recommissioning.

r542.diagnosis: BACnet service/configuration issue on local subnet
r542.action: Verify BACnet/IP enabled state, UDP port, device instance, and local firewall.

r543.action: Investigate bindings, object references, server discovery cache, and application configuration.

r544.action: Review packet captures/logs and server/device discovery settings for intermittent or application-level issues.

r545.diagnosis: BBMD, foreign-device, routing, or firewall issue
r545.action: Correct BDT/FDT entries, broadcast distribution, UDP port rules, and routing.

r560.diagnosis: Electrical noise or grounding issue is likely
r560.action: Check grounding and shield termination against the trunk design, separation of the communications cable from power and high-current conductors, and induced noise on the communications cable. Confirm the specified shielded twisted-pair cable is used.

r568.diagnosis: VFD-related interference is a candidate requiring verification
r568.action: Check VFD grounding and the shielding and routing of the VFD output cable. Keep the communications cable away from VFD output and line conductors, and cross them at right angles where unavoidable. Verify the communications shield is terminated only as the trunk design requires and is not bonded to the VFD chassis by accident. Review line reactor, output filter, and EMC requirements in the VFD manual. When it is safe and permitted, confirm by stopping the VFD and checking whether the drops stop. Coordinate with the VFD owner or electrical contractor before changing VFD settings or wiring.

r561.action: Measure voltage during events, verify transformer loading, grounding, and power-supply health.

r562.diagnosis: Intermittent network issue not yet isolated
r562.action: Review event logs and trends; inspect connectors, switch errors, trunk statistics, and environmental conditions.

r563.diagnosis: Single device or segment is intermittent
r563.action: Inspect local power, terminals, transceiver, cable segment, address, and device logs.

r581.diagnosis: Communication values match end to end
r581.action: Investigate sequence logic, graphics presentation, alarms, units, and operator expectations.

q601.question: What VAV symptom are you troubleshooting?

q603.question: Is the VAV occupied and cooling airflow setpoint above zero?

q604.question: Is actual airflow below airflow setpoint?

q605.question: Is damper command high but measured airflow remains low?

q606.question: Is reheat active or the discharge temperature high?

q611.question: Is cooling airflow/damper command higher than expected?

q612.question: Is reheat command present and discharge temperature increasing?

q620.question: Is the AHU that serves this VAV running and delivering airflow to the duct system?
q620.notes: Confirm actual upstream operation, not only an AHU command. Use fan proof, duct static, and a field airflow check where available.

q621.question: Is the VAV damper commanded open?

q630.question: Which Schneider Electric VAV controller arrangement is installed?
q630.notes: MPV and RPV use built-in damper actuators. MPC and RPC require a separately hardwired actuator. Route to AO-8 only when a Central IO AO-8 module is physically installed.

q640.question: What type of reheat control is used?

q622.question: Is airflow present at the VAV inlet or upstream branch duct, with adequate inlet pressure for the box to deliver its setpoint?
q622.notes: Check at the box inlet or nearest approved test location. Do not assume that AHU operation guarantees airflow at this branch.

q623.question: Can AHU fan proof, duct static, and an upstream field airflow check be confirmed?

q624.question: Is the airflow sensor reading believable compared with a field measurement?

q631.question: Does the MPV or RPV built-in actuator position and physical damper rotation follow the commanded position?
q631.notes: MPV and RPV have built-in actuators, so there is no separate field actuator signal wire or AO-8 module-health check for the damper output.

q632.question: For the MPC or RPC, does the onboard analog output command and measured signal at the hardwired actuator input agree?
q632.notes: MPC and RPC require a separately hardwired actuator. Use the controller onboard-output workflow unless the project actually uses a Central AO-8 module.

q633.question: After checking labels, drawings or point references, which controller and actuator arrangement can you confirm?

q634.question: With adequate inlet airflow, does the physical damper travel freely through the required range and is linkage/shaft engagement correct?

q635.question: Does the unit/controller-reported damper command and feedback change together, without an active local override or fault?

r602.diagnosis: Upstream AHU is not providing airflow
r602.action: Troubleshoot the serving AHU, fan enable/proof, safeties, duct static, smoke/fire dampers, and upstream distribution before condemning the VAV.

r603.diagnosis: No airflow or inadequate pressure is reaching the VAV inlet
r603.action: Inspect the upstream branch for closed balancing/fire/smoke dampers, disconnected or collapsed duct, blockage, leakage, incorrect tap, or insufficient AHU static pressure.

r604.diagnosis: Upstream air-system condition is not confirmed
r604.action: Confirm the serving AHU identity, fan proof, duct static, and airflow at an upstream test point before testing the VAV controller or actuator.

r605.diagnosis: MPV or RPV built-in damper actuator is not following command
r605.action: Verify controller mode, application, actuator calibration, shaft engagement, mechanical obstruction, and controller faults. Do not look for an AO-8 module unless one is actually installed.

r606.action: Identify the exact controller and actuator from labels, drawings, submittals, and EBO references before electrical testing. Avoid assuming a Central IO module exists.

r607.diagnosis: Damper command and mechanical travel appear normal
r607.action: Verify airflow pickup tubing, box factor/K-factor, inlet pressure, balancing, minimum/maximum airflow settings, duct condition, and downstream restrictions.

r608.action: Inspect shaft engagement, set screws, linkage, blade obstruction, actuator mounting, and full-stroke setup. Repair mechanics before changing the control sequence.

r609.diagnosis: Third-party or network-controlled damper path is not responding
r609.action: Verify local controller faults, network command/feedback, local override, output configuration, actuator power, and OEM sequence. Use the exact unit documentation.

r601.diagnosis: VAV controls appear to be responding
r601.action: Verify system supply-air temperature and static pressure, upstream AHU availability, box inlet pressure, airflow pickup tubing orientation/condition, damper/linkage travel, design min/max airflow, balancing, duct restrictions, and reheat valve/stage operation. Compare actual field measurements with design values before changing control parameters.

q701.question: What AHU symptom are you troubleshooting?

q702.question: Is the AHU enabled by schedule/occupancy?

q703.question: Are all safeties and interlocks normal?

q710.question: Are supply-air and mixed-air temperatures accurate?

q711.question: Is cooling enabled and the valve/compressor command increasing?

q712.question: What cooling output type is used?

q720.question: Are supply-air and heating-water/air temperatures accurate?

q721.question: Is heating enabled and command increasing?

q722.question: What heating output type is used?

q730.question: Is static-pressure reading accurate compared with a field measurement?

q731.question: Is fan-speed command changing to maintain setpoint?

q713.question: Is the chilled-water/refrigeration source available and are required pumps, valves, and equipment proven?

q714.question: Is cooling medium reaching the AHU coil, or are DX circuits available, with expected entering conditions?

q723.question: Is the heating source available and are required pumps, valves, steam pressure, or electric-heat permissives proven?

r1502.action: Verify controller health, output object, priority array, operating mode, safeties, setpoints, bindings, and application logic.

r509.action: Record the exact model, EBO/firmware version, hub connection status and available diagnostics. Use applicable manufacturer documentation and escalate for technical review; do not apply MS/TP baud-rate or BACnet/IP broadcast checks by default.

r305.action: Record module status and LED indication; verify specified power, terminal-base seating, Central IO bus and controller/module configuration. Establish module health before voltage or current-output testing. Do not infer a current-loop fault before identifying the output type.

r587.action: Use the exact controller and sensor documentation to compare the field measurement with the configured input type, channel, units and scale. Isolate wiring and use approved test methods where authorized. Do not assume a UI-16 module or 10k Type II sensor is installed.

r588.diagnosis: Value differs between originating device and receiving system
r588.action: Verify protocol-specific object/register mapping, units, conversion, update timestamp and quality/status. For Modbus, verify the exact manufacturer register map and data representation; do not assume addressing offsets or byte/word order.

r589.diagnosis: Originating network device reports an incorrect value
r589.action: Investigate the originating device sensor, configuration, local process and manufacturer diagnostics before changing receiving-system mapping.

r586.action: Trace the source values, units, calculation, bindings and update timestamps. Compare with the approved sequence and observed process before an authorized change.

r585.diagnosis: Required evidence or point-source identity is unavailable
r585.action: Record what is known and what is missing. Obtain the point reference, device model, signal type, measurement and timestamp before selecting a fault diagnosis. Do not treat unavailable evidence as a failed test.

r564.diagnosis: Restart or power evidence is insufficient
r564.action: Record the drop time, Automation Server online state, status-light observation and available restart/event records. Obtain authorized input-power evidence where needed. Do not diagnose a trunk, power or firmware fault solely because records are unavailable.

q526.question: Do available MS/TP traffic statistics or an approved capture show communication errors or retries?
q526.notes: Online status alone is not proof of a healthy trunk. Record available statistics/capture and observation interval. Missing capture evidence does not prove healthy communications. Continue physical-layer checks without inventing an error threshold.

r526.diagnosis: MS/TP fault remains unisolated after sectional testing
r526.action: Review the recorded trunk configuration, statistics/capture, device power and firmware. Compare with a documented known-good segment/device where approved. Escalate with evidence; failure to isolate a segment does not prove an individual transceiver is faulty.

q1701.question: Does the Modbus RTU device have correct power and a normal local operating state?

q1702.question: Do serial settings and device address match the configured Modbus RTU client and exact device documentation?
q1702.notes: Verify the applicable baud rate, parity, stop bits and device address. These are Modbus RTU checks, not Modbus TCP checks. Do not apply BACnet MAC, Max Master or token-management rules.

q1703.question: Does the installed serial wiring match the documented interface and topology?
q1703.notes: Identify the actual serial interface and exact product requirements before polarity, termination, shield or isolation checks.

q1704.question: Does a documented supported request receive a valid response?

q1705.question: Does the returned value match the manufacturer register map and independent process evidence?

r1701.diagnosis: Modbus device local power or operating-state issue
r1701.action: Resolve the observed local power/status condition using exact-model documentation before communications testing.

r1702.action: Document the mismatch and correct only the approved device/client serial settings and address. Retest a documented supported request.

r1703.action: Document and correct wiring against the approved design and device manual. Isolate power and sensitive electronics as required; do not add termination arbitrarily.

r1704.diagnosis: Modbus RTU response fault remains unisolated
r1704.action: Record request, response/exception or timeout, timestamp, device address and serial settings. Review supported requests, polling and exact-model diagnostics. Sectional isolation requires approval.

r1705.diagnosis: Modbus request and value appear consistent with reviewed evidence
r1705.action: Continue with application bindings, timestamps, units and approved sequence expectations. This does not prove all registers or intermittent operation are healthy.

r1706.diagnosis: Modbus mapping or data interpretation requires verification
r1706.action: Compare the exact register reference, supported function, data type, scale, signedness and byte/word order with the device manufacturer register map. Record raw and interpreted values. Do not guess address offsets or conversion conventions.

q1801.question: Does the Modbus TCP device have correct power and a normal local operating state?

q1802.question: Do physical link and IP/network evidence support reachability of the configured Modbus TCP endpoint?
q1802.notes: Verify the configured endpoint and approved network design. Ping alone does not establish Modbus service availability. No serial baud-rate, parity or stop-bit checks belong in this branch.

q1803.question: Are the configured TCP service endpoint and any required unit identifier consistent with exact device or gateway documentation?
q1803.notes: If a TCP-to-RTU gateway is installed, treat its downstream serial segment as a separately identified Modbus RTU path, not as a serial setting on the TCP connection.

q1804.question: Does a documented supported Modbus TCP request receive a valid response?

q1805.question: Does the returned value match the manufacturer register map and independent process evidence?

r1801.diagnosis: Modbus TCP IP path requires investigation
r1801.action: Record link and addressing evidence; review approved switch, VLAN, routing and firewall configuration with the network owner. Do not change network settings without authorization.

r1802.diagnosis: Modbus TCP endpoint or gateway configuration mismatch
r1802.action: Verify configured endpoint, service and applicable unit identifier against exact-model documentation. Coordinate approved corrections with the device/network owner.

r1803.diagnosis: Modbus TCP service response fault remains unisolated
r1803.action: Record request, response/exception or timeout, endpoint and timestamp. Review exact-model service availability, supported requests, polling and gateway status where installed. Do not route to RTU unless a downstream serial segment is identified.

r135.action: Record sensor part number, input type, configured curve and reference temperature. Use the approved sensor and controller documentation for resistance, wiring and tolerance checks. No generic resistance table or fault diagnosis is assumed.
